lines.beaver_en: Hello. Are you here for foreigner registration?
lines.en: Yes, hello. I came to register.

lines.beaver_en: Okay, may I have your name?
Mr. Hans, are you Japanese, by any chance?
lines.learner: 아니요, 일본 사람이 아닙니다. 독일 사람이에요.
lines.en: No, I'm not Japanese. I'm German.
lines.roman: Aniyo, ilbon sarami animnida. Dogil saramieyo.

lines.beaver: 아, 독일이요. 한국에는 어떻게 오시게 되었어요?
lines.beaver_en: Ah, Germany. How did you come to Korea?
lines.beaver_roman: A, dogiriyo. Hangugeneun eotteoke osige doeeosseoyo?
lines.en: I came last year for work.

lines.beaver_en: What do you do while living in Korea?
lines.en: I study Korean while working at a company.

lines.beaver: 그럼 이 서류에 국적과 주소를 써 주세요.
lines.beaver_en: Then please write your nationality and address on this form.
lines.beaver_roman: Geureom i seoryue gukjeokgwa jusoreul sseo juseyo.
lines.learner: 네. 국적은 독일, 주소는 서울 마포구예요.
lines.en: Okay. Nationality is Germany, address is Mapo-gu, Seoul.
lines.roman: Ne. Gukjeogeun dogil, jusoneun seoul mapoguyeyo.

lines.beaver_en: Please write the neighborhood and lot number too. And your sex.
Okay. Do you have family living with you?
lines.en: I have a wife. She's Thai.

lines.beaver_en: Then your wife needs to register separately too.
lines.en: Yes, my wife is filling out a form over there.

lines.beaver: 네, 다 됐어요. 2주 후에 카드 받으러 오세요.
lines.beaver_en: Okay, all done. Come pick up your card in two weeks.
lines.beaver_roman: Ne, da dwaesseoyo. Iju hue kadeu badeureo oseyo.
